deep.reconstruction:
Context: in these 1974 notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'tame' (modérée) topology on a space X. This is a family F of admissible subsets subject to axioms a)–f), which are introduced on earlier pages not shown here. On the previous page he proved two things. First, a set that is locally a union of leaves of a partition into strata is globally one. Second, for A in the restricted class F_U, each A∩X_i is clopen in X_i∩U, so A is a union of connected components of the sets X_i∩U. A counterexample (ℝ stratified as {0} ∪ ℝ*, with ℝ+ not in F) shows the converse fails.

This page has two parts.

(1) Study of axiom f), apparently a local-finiteness / local-connectedness condition on connected components of members of F.
- f) is stable under restriction to an open set U that itself belongs to F, but clearly not under restriction to an arbitrary open U.
- For arbitrary U one only gets the following. If A ∈ F_U is locally closed in U (closed in some smaller open V ⊂ U), then A is locally connected, so its connected components are open in A.
- If A is moreover locally compact (e.g. if X is), the components form a locally finite family in A, hence in V, since A is closed in V.
- He then asks whether the family is locally finite in U itself.
- A crossed-out attempt follows. It seems to define an 'F-locally closed' Z ∈ F as one where every x ∈ U has an open neighbourhood V ∈ F_U with A∩V ∈ F and A∩V having only finitely many connected components.

(2) Sheaf-theoretic reformulation.
- Let 𝒢_X be the sheaf of germs of subsets of X (U ↦ P(U)), and let F̲ ⊂ 𝒢_X be a subsheaf satisfying a)–d).
- New axiom e): for every open U and every descending chain X_1 ⊃ X_2 ⊃ … of closed subsets of U lying in Γ(U,F̲), with each X_{n+1} rare (nowhere dense) in X_n, the chain is locally finite on U. Hence ∩X_i = ∅.
- The next page adds the consequences: for every quasi-compact K, some X_i misses K. Γ(X,F̲) satisfies a)–d), and e) if X is quasi-compact. The strengthened version e_n) defines 'F̲-dimension ≤ n'.
- The next page also remarks that F̲ can be strictly larger than the sheaf generated by its global sections. The example is the analytic sheaf on a 2-dimensional complex torus without non-constant meromorphic functions.

Purpose: to set up a localizable (sheafified) axiomatics of tame subsets with a dimension theory defined by chains of nowhere-dense closed tame subsets. This is a forerunner of o-minimal / 'tame topology' axiomatics.
errors: The deduction 'A locally closed ⇒ A locally connected' is not justified on the page itself. It must rely on axiom f) (or a)–d)) as formulated on an earlier page, which is not visible here.

The question of local finiteness of the components in U (rather than V) is left open; the attempted definition is crossed out. The obvious counterexample type, a set accumulating on the boundary of V inside U (e.g. sin(1/x)-type, or infinitely many components accumulating at a point of U∖V), shows the answer is in general no without extra hypotheses. This is not stated.
Locally finite decreasing chain ⇒ empty intersection is correct, but is only meaningful for an infinite chain. No strictness is needed. Fine.

ideas.what: Axiomatic class of tame subsets, with stability of axioms under restriction to tame open sets but not arbitrary open sets
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of o-minimal / tame structures to definable open subsets; definable vs non-definable opens
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86); Shiota (axiomatic 𝔛-sets, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (topologie modérée) discusses the programme in general terms, not these specific axioms

ideas.what: Local finiteness of connected components of a locally closed tame set (finiteness of components locally)
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness of definably connected components / local finiteness in o-minimal and subanalytic geometry

ideas.what: Tame sets as a subsheaf F̲ of the sheaf of germs of subsets of X
ideas.modern_name: Locally definable / sheaf of tame sets; cf. locally definable spaces, o-minimal sheaves, subanalytic site
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (locally semialgebraic spaces, 1985); Kashiwara–Schapira (subanalytic sheaves, 2001); Edmundo et al. (o-minimal sheaf theory)

ideas.what: Axiom e)/e_n): chains of closed tame sets, each nowhere dense in the previous, are locally finite / of bounded length; defines 'F̲-dimension'
ideas.modern_name: Dimension via frontier/nowhere-dense chains (Krull-type topological dimension); o-minimal dimension with dim(fr A) < dim A
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimal dimension theory)

ideas.what: Sheaf of tame sets need not be generated by its global sections (analytic torus example, on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Locally vs globally definable sets; non-algebraic compact complex tori
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard complex-analytic fact; the use as a tame-topology example is unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1974 sheafified axiomatics of tame topology: a subsheaf of the sheaf of germs of subsets satisfying Boolean/topological axioms plus a dimension axiom by chains of nowhere-dense closed tame sets. It predates o-minimality and the axiomatic frameworks of Shiota and Delfs–Knebusch, and was never developed or published in this form.
missed.quote: Soit F̲ un sous-faisceau du faisceau 𝒢_X des germes de parties de X. On suppose que F̲ satisfait a) b) c) d), et de plus e) ... X_{n+1} rare dans X_n. Alors la suite des X_i est loc finie sur U
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a local (non-first-order) axiomatization of tameness, applicable to analytic or non-definable situations. It is close in spirit to the subanalytic site and to locally o-minimal / o-minimal sheaf theory, and it documents Grothendieck's priority in thinking of tameness sheaf-theoretically.

missed.claim: Open question whether components of a locally closed tame set in U are locally finite in U, not just in a smaller open V where the set is closed; the attempted fix is crossed out.
missed.quote: Elle est-elle loc. finie dans U ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It corresponds to the known issue of restricting tame structures to non-tame opens, handled in modern theory by requiring definable opens.

deep.surprise_reason: The sheaf-theoretic formulation of tame topology with a chain-based dimension axiom in 1974 is a notable unpublished detail anticipating o-minimal and subanalytic-site ideas. The page's actual content, however, is preliminary and mostly routine point-set topology, with an open question left unresolved.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'la condition la condition f)' is a duplication; the image has 'la condition f).'
'On a seulement, dans,' should probably read 'On a seulement, ceci,' or similar; the word is illegible but 'dans' does not fit.
'Elle est-elle loc. finie dans U ?' — the image shows 'Elle' with 'est ≡' inserted above and the underlined phrase 'loc. finie dans U ?'
The crossed-out block should begin 'Ceci n'est vrai que ...'/'Ceci n'[a] ...'; 'A = ℤ, avec ℤ ∈ F' is more plausibly 'A = Z, avec Z ∈ F', where Z is a generic letter, not the integers.
In the second part, the struck word before 'e)' looks like 'fonctions' or 'f)' replaced by 'e)'; 'de plus' is inserted above.
Margin note is largely illegible; it plausibly refers to restriction to an arbitrary open set versus an open set in F, not a confident reading.
